name: IBBIS (International Biosecurity and Biosafety Initiative for Science)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: a pandemic kills people everywhere and the future lost is everyone's, so the result is spread by world population.
summary: IBBIS, a Geneva foundation launched in 2024 out of NTI | bio, works to stop DNA synthesis being used to make pandemic pathogens: a free open-source screening tool (commec) synthesis providers install, a screening evaluation portal with NIST, two expert consortia on screening standards, the Global DNA Synthesis Map, policy engagement and in-country workshops. This model of all its work in 2025 comes to about {{result}} years of healthy life per $1,000, from {{low}} to {{high}} on its plausible range: each dollar is valued as a typical project's cut in the forecast pandemic risk (Rethink Priorities' cross-cause model; the Existential Risk Persuasion Tournament's experts), deaths valued like every death (a COVID-scale pandemic's at COVID's age mix) and the future lost counted only where you count lives that never start (0% by default). IBBIS publishes no accounts, so its spending (about $2.3M) is built from its staff; the result per dollar barely depends on it. The biggest uncertainties are the years a cut counts, the discount rate and how much a typical dollar cuts the risk (the range runs ten times either way); the one branch is discounted for missing data, since no outcome of the work on the risk is measured.

sections.title: Other outcomes, in this model's unit
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for outcomes in more than one unit (docs/normalization.md 2.6): each outcome is counted in its own unit (units of value for income and deaths, WELLBYs for life satisfaction, tonnes of CO₂e, chicken pain days) and put into this model's unit by its unit's conversion over this unit's, which the headline's conversion cancels. So each moves only with its own sliders, exactly as in a model of its own unit. The rows are fixed; don't edit them.

rows.explainer: IBBIS publishes no accounts or budget (a Swiss foundation, which need not publish them; its site, annual letter and the Swiss register give none), so its 2025 spending is built from its staff. The annual letter says it "effectively doubled its core staff" in 2025, to a full-time team of 10 by the year's end: about 5 at the start, so 7.5 on average if the hires came through the year. Our judgment, 5 (hires late in the year) to 10 (all early).

Suffering of the farmed animals the people of that future would eat, in healthy years
rows.formula: -((cost_total * ai_cost_share / 1e6 * ai_future_per_million * ai_discounted_years) + (cost_total * bio_cost_share / 1e6 * bio_future_per_million * bio_discounted_years) + (cost_total * nuclear_cost_share / 1e6 * nuclear_future_per_million * nuclear_discounted_years) + (pol_wins * pol_p_success * pol_relative_cut * pol_future_per_year * pol_discounted_years) + (fb_work_dollars / 1e6 * fb_credit_share * fb_future_per_million * pv_annuity_due(1, $discount_rate, years_of_impact))) * $lives_added * $animal_dalys_per_person_year_world
rows.explainer: A future kept is also every animal raised to feed it: each future person-year at the suffering of the animals an average person eats in a year today (docs/normalization.md 2.25). Suffering always counts, whatever lives that never start count; the farmed animals' own good days count where you set them to. Held at today's diet: no forecast of what people will eat is used.

rows.label: Pandemic field work: how far the typical project's effect applies
rows.explainer: Its outputs show some uptake, but on balance a little less than a typical project's: commec, the free open-source screening tool, is in use by synthesis providers (Dynegene and the Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology in China, a Latin American provider screening every order) and met industry standards in independent benchmarking in 2025; the screening evaluation portal it runs with NIST did more than 15 evaluations; its two consortia drew about 30 and over 60 experts and its draft guide implements ISO 20688-2. But adoption is a handful of providers (most orders are screened by large providers' own tools), screening stops only actors who order DNA, and the standards and the EU Biotech Act were not yet in force. 0.8, our judgment, 0.3 to 1.2.

rows.label: Pandemic field work: this charity's share of the resources behind it
rows.explainer: IBBIS's share of the resources behind its outputs: its consortia run on members' unpaid expert time (about 30 in the DSSC, over 60 in the SBRC), the 2025 study on AI-redesigned toxins was led by Microsoft with Twist and other DNA synthesis companies (Wittmann et al., Science 390:82, doi 10.1126/science.adu8578), NIST writes the evaluation portal's test sets, and the map and workshops had co-hosts. About 90 experts giving 2 to 5% of a year at a work-year's cost is $0.5M to $1.1M beside IBBIS's $2.3M; fellows' time paid by their own programmes adds a little. The consortium members that screen orders are also the ones who would take the standards up: the part of their time spent adopting, a third of the members' $0.5M to $1.1M by our judgment (not derived: most of the time counted is writing standards; the 2 to 5% of a year per expert is our judgment too), is under the mobiliser's share, not in this one (docs/normalization.md 2.24). 0.8, our judgment, 0.55 to 0.95. The Nuclear Threat Initiative's 2025 grant to IBBIS ($38,343, its Form 990's Schedule F) is inside IBBIS's spending here, so it lowers nothing; the screening tool's development under NTI's incubation (2019 to 2023) belongs to those years, not to 2025.

rows.label: Benefits not modelled, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Good beyond the pandemics counted: screening also flags orders for toxins (the 2025 study redesigned ricin and other toxins), whose misuse kills few rather than starts a pandemic, and the customer-screening forms and synthesis map help export-control authorities with licensing. +5%, from 0 to +15%, our judgment.

rows.label: Harm: speeding up dangerous capabilities, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: A typical project's chance of backfiring is already in the shared cut. IBBIS builds no capabilities: its tools and standards only screen orders. 0, down to −2% if screening rules slow legitimate research enough to push it to providers that don't screen. Our judgment.

rows.label: Harm: information hazards and attention, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Beyond a typical project's backfire: the Global DNA Synthesis Map shows publicly which providers screen and where no rules apply, which also tells a would-be attacker where to order; the 2025 study showed AI tools could redesign toxins past screening, though the tools were patched before publication and the sensitive data is behind tiered access. −3%, from −10% to 0, our judgment.
